raw_response:
I’m still planting cotton on all 10.1 mu this year. I’ve done this a long time, and on my land cotton is what I know best. Wheat and maize turn over too fast and need more rush in June, but with just two people at home, cotton is easier for us to manage across the season. I have middle school education, so I do listen when township technicians talk about spacing and fertilizer, but in the end I still go by what I’ve seen on my own fields. If I feed cotton too little, the plants stay weak and the bolls are small. If I push too much fertilizer, especially nitrogen, it grows too much leaf and can lodge or delay. So this year I’ll do a moderate rate, not the highest.

At the start I’ll prepare the land with rotary tillage and ridge it properly, then plant in mid to late April, depending on soil temperature. I’ll use hybrid cotton seed from the local dealer, the kind most people around here buy, because emergence is better and yield is steadier than saved seed. For fertilizer, I’ll put most of the phosphorus and potassium down as base fertilizer, with part of the nitrogen too, then topdress nitrogen later around budding and early flowering. Since I have well water, I’ll irrigate if the spring is dry and again at the key stages, but I won’t water too many times because pumping costs money. Pesticide I’ll use according to what I see in the field, mainly for weeds early and insects later if pressure comes up. My expectation is not to chase the very highest yield, just a solid crop with controlled spending.
